evidence: Opened in 1969, this theatre stands as a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Vietnam, its majestic name, Thăng Long, commemorating the relocation of the capital by King Lý Thái Tổ, who moved the seat of power to this strategic location in the early 11th century. The name Thăng Long itself evokes the legendary moment when a golden dragon soared into the sky, symbolizing the ascension of the city to a new era of prosperity and cultural significance.

The theatre’s location, adjacent to the historic Hoàn Kiếm Lake, underscores its importance within the heart of Hanoi, a city steeped in ancient traditions and modern vibrancy. As visitors approach the theatre, they are greeted by the serene beauty of the lake, framed by the lush greenery of the surrounding area, which includes the iconic Ngoc Son Temple and the bustling streets of the Old Quarter.
